title: Protocol for in vivo and ex vivo assessments of glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in mouse islet β cells
protocol: Dissolve D-glucose in deionized water.
Sterilize the solution by filtration.
Dissolve heparin in saline solution.
Sterilize this solution by filtration.
Sterilize three-way Y connector with 75% ethanol solution.
Connect two joints of the three-way Y connector to 0.3048 mm ID silicone tubing.
Stock one of the silicone tubes with a 10 mm long stainless plug.
Flush the other silicone tube with D-glucose solution.
Withdraw D-glucose solution into a 1 mL syringe.
Join the syringe and 0.3048 mm ID silicone tube with a flat needle.
Weigh the pre-fasted mouse.
Narcotize the mouse in the anesthesia chamber.
Transfer the experimental mouse to the operating table.
Keep narcosis status with isoflurane through mask.
Remove the plug in the back of the mouse's neck.
Inject heparin up to 50 μL into the mouse.
Connect the flat end protruding from the mouse's skin to the unoccupied joint of the three-way Y connector.
Transfer the mouse to the fixator.
Acclimate the mouse for about 30 min.
Adjust the infusion rate according to mouse weights.
Set the initial glucose solution rate at 30 mg/kg/min.
Measure blood glucose level with a glucose meter through the tail vein.
Collect a fasting blood sample.
Turn on the syringe pump.
Collect blood samples at 2, 5, and 10 min.
Estimate insulin levels after the experiment.
Draw the insulin secretion curve when finished the experiment.
Calculate the area under curve (AUC) for first-phase insulin secretion.
Adjust glucose infusion rate (GIR) to clamp blood glucose level at 306 mg/dL (± 18 mg/dL).
Record blood glucose levels and GIR in Table 1 during the experiment.
Collect blood samples every 10 min.
Estimate insulin levels after the experiment.
Draw the insulin secretion curve when finished the experiment.
Calculate the area under curve (AUC) for second-phase insulin secretion.
Stop the pump if blood glucose level is clamped and perfusion rate reaches a stable level within 30 min.
Disassemble the infusion device.
Insert a stainless plug into the end of the silastic tube on the mouse.
Transfer each mouse to their own cage for another 3 days to recover.
Centrifuge blood samples at 675 g for 30 min.
Collect serum carefully from centrifuged blood samples.
Store collected serum samples at –20°C for up to 4 weeks, or at –80°C for up to 2 months if not detected in time.
Measure insulin levels with an insulin ELISA kit.
Use at least 3 μL of serum per replicate for measurement.
Dilute serum samples to 5 μL using saline solution when necessary.
Ensure that at least 15 μL of whole blood is collected for serum isolation.
Store collected blood samples on ice before centrifuging.
Optional: Centrifuge whole blood sample from donor mouse at 4°C, 450 g, for 20 min if the volume of blood collection exceeds 10% of total body weight (about 2 ml per 25 g).
Discard plasma and platelets after centrifugation.
Measure the volume of red-blood-cell with a pipette.
Wash red-blood-cell with 10 U/mL heparin saline solution.
Centrifuge at 4°C, 450 g, for 20 minutes.
Resuspend the cells in heparin saline solution to match the volume measured previously.
Store the resuspended red-blood-cell on ice before use.
Connect the red-blood-cell in syringe and mouse with a four-way X connector.
Transfuse at a rate of 2 μL/min.
Narcotize the mouse by intraperitoneal injection of 2% pentobarbital sodium solution (40 mg/kg body weight).
Transfer the anesthetized mouse to the operating table.
Disinfect the abdominal skin with ethanol solution.
Cut the skin and muscular layer along the midabdominal line.
Separate the major duodenal papilla from the duodenum using fine tweezers.
Ligate the bile duct.
Separate the major papilla from the duodenum.
Ligate the bile duct near the liver.
Insert the needle into the bile duct until it is inserted at least 2 mm.
Begin to perfuse digestion buffer from the common bile duct proximal to the liver to the pancreas.
Strip off the filled pancreas from the bottom, up along the direction of the intestines to the stomach and spleen.
Transfer the pancreas to a sterilized 50 mL centrifuge tube in an ice-bath.
Cut up the pancreatic tissue into pieces carefully if not filled with digestion buffer.
Add 2–3 mL collagenase to the centrifuge tube to reach 5 mL volume.
Transfer the tube to a 37°C shaking water bath for 18 minutes.
Remove the tube and vortex at 700 g for 10 seconds.
If digestion is not homogenous, digest tissue for another 2–5 minutes.
Add 10 mL HBSS with 10% CBS to stop digestion.
Vortex the tube after adding HBSS.
Filter undigested tissue through a 0.600 mm bore diameter sieve (30 mesh).
Collect filtered mixture in a new 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 385 g for 2 minutes.
Discard supernatant and add another 10 mL HBSS to resuspend sediment.
Repeat centrifugation at 385 g for 2 minutes.
Add 5 mL histopaque and resuspend the sediment.
Transfer mixture to a sterilized glass 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Add 5 mL HBSS slowly along the wall of the tube with a syringe.
Centrifuge at 770 g for 20 minutes with a uniform acceleration rate of 9 g and a uniform deceleration rate of 2 g.
Pre-cool the centrifuge to 4°C before use.
Remove the mid-layer of the supernatant with a pipettor to a 10 cm dish containing 8 mL stop solution.
Add 8 μL DTZ solution into the dish.
Stain islets at 37°C for 1 minute.
Pick up the stained islets under the stereoscopic microscope and transfer them to a 10 cm dish containing 10 mL stop solution.
Transfer the islets again to a 10 cm dish containing 10 mL culture medium.
Allow the islets to recover for 8–12 hours.
Transfer 30–50 individual islets randomly to a 3.5 cm dish containing 500 μL PBS.
Add 1 mL FDA/PI solution and stain the islets for 20 minutes at 20–25°C in the dark.
Discard the supernatant after staining.
Wash the islets with PBS for 5 minutes.
Repeat the wash three times.
Transfer stained islets to a 3.5 cm dish containing 1.5 mL PBS.
Observe and photograph islets under a fluorescence microscope using excitation light of 536 nm for PI and 494 nm for FDA.
Culture islets in tissue culture dishes for suspension cell to keep them suspended.
Prepare perfusion buffers including low glucose buffer, high glucose buffer, and high potassium buffer, incubate at 37°C water bath.
Assemble perfusion device including syringe pump, injection syringe, silastic tube, infusion warmer, three-way valve, syringe filter, and needle for blood taking.
Pick up 120 islets per group and incubate them in low glucose buffer at 37°C for 1 hour.
Transfer the islets into a syringe filter after incubation.
Connect the syringe filter to the injection syringe with low glucose buffer using the three-way valve.
Adjust perfusion rate to 125 μL/min.
Turn on the syringe pump to perfuse islets with low glucose buffer for 20 minutes.
Perfuse with low glucose buffer for 10 minutes.
Collect the perfusate every 1 minute into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Switch the three-way valve to connect the syringe filter and injection syringe with high glucose buffer.
Turn on the syringe pump loaded with high glucose buffer.
Simultaneously turn off the syringe pump loaded with low glucose buffer.
Perfuse with high glucose buffer for 25 minutes.
Collect the perfusate every 1 minute into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Switch the three-way valve again to connect syringe filter and injection syringe with low glucose perfusion buffer.
Turn off the syringe pump loaded with high glucose buffer.
Simultaneously turn on the syringe pump loaded with low glucose buffer for re-equilibration of islets for 20 minutes.
Replace the high glucose buffer with high potassium buffer and relevant silastic tube during re-equilibration.
Continue to perfuse low glucose buffer for 10 minutes.
Collect the perfusate every 1 minute into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Switch the three-way valve to connect the syringe filter and injection syringe with high potassium buffer.
Perfuse with high potassium buffer for 15 minutes.
Collect the perfusate every 1 minute into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Turn off all of the syringe pumps.
Store perfusion samples at -20°C up to 4 weeks or at -80°C up to 2 months.
Flush out islets from the islet deposit chambers using 5 mL low glucose buffer.
Flush the syringe three times and collect flushing buffer in a 10 cm dish.
Count the number of islets and collect them in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Extract the insulin content with 1 mL extraction buffer at 4°C for 12 h.
Centrifuge the extraction buffer at 4°C, 900 g for 5 min, and collect 500 μL supernatant.
Store the samples at –20°C for up to 4 weeks or at –80°C for up to 2 months.
Discard the liquid after centrifuging the remaining islets at 300 g for 5 min.
Extract total DNA or protein and measure the relative concentration.
Calibrate insulin secretion capability of each sample based on DNA or protein concentration.
Equilibrate the islets in low glucose buffer and incubate for 1 h.
Rotate the plate in the same direction to gather the islets into the center of the well.
Remove the fluid from the edge of the well and discard it.
Add 200 μL low glucose buffer and incubate for 1 h.
Collect 150 μL supernatant as the low glucose-stimulated insulin secretion sample.
Discard the remaining buffer.
Add 200 μL high glucose buffer and incubate for 1 h.
Collect 150 μL supernatant as the high glucose-stimulated insulin secretion sample.
Discard the remaining buffer.
Add 200 μL extraction buffer and incubate at 4°C for 12 h to extract the insulin content.
